task.goal: Produce a numbered educational 'tips' carousel: a title cover slide with a two-tone keyword accent, a run of numbered tip slides each showing exactly one wrong(X)/right(check) example pair, and a closing engagement-CTA slide inviting comments, likes, and saves.
task.success_condition: The title slide's second line carries a visibly distinct accent color on the emphasis keyword; every tip slide shows a two-digit sequential number (01, 02, 03...) paired with one clearly differentiated wrong/right example (not two near-identical images); numbering has no gaps or repeats across the run; and the closing slide shows the comment/heart/save icon row beneath a direct engagement prompt, not a link-out or follow prompt.
task.atomic_boundary: One design/skill topic becomes one short numbered-tips carousel (title cover + N numbered tip slides + one closing engagement slide). No single-frame quote graphic, no video or motion, no product/wishlist grid, and no off-platform link-in-bio call to action folded into the closing slide.

source_expression_moment.description: The skill/topic and the specific numbered tips content to render (one wrong/right lesson per tip).

voice_context.description: Source handle/voice and title-accent styling reference used for rendering decisions.

carousel_slide_sequence.description: An ordered set of production-ready slide frames: one title cover, N numbered wrong/right tip slides, and one closing engagement-CTA slide.

activative_input.hidden_pressure: The viewer has scrolled past dozens of 'tips' carousels that all promise value and deliver vague platitudes. This one must earn the save by making each numbered tip's wrong/right contrast legible at a glance, not by adding more explanatory text.
activative_input.stance: Instructional, direct, confident -- numbered authority over decorative flourish.
stakes: the wrong/right pair reads as visually identical and the lesson fails to land
the numbering skips or repeats and the list loses credibility as a complete reference
the closing slide is skipped or ignored because it reads as generic filler rather than a genuine invitation to participate
identity_urges: walk away with one concrete, usable rule per slide
feel competent enough to apply the tip immediately
activative_input.participation_design: The viewer swipes through numbered tips, absorbs one wrong/right contrast per slide, and on the final slide is prompted to comment their own tip, like, and save the post for later reference.
activative_input.intended_reaction: The viewer saves the carousel as a reference guide and comments their own tip, growing the post's reach through genuine participation rather than a redirect off-platform.
activative_input.smallest_useful_commitment: Swipe to the next numbered tip.
wrong_reading_locks: Do not ship a wrong(X)/right(check) example pair that is visually indistinguishable -- the reference specimen's placeholder pair uses near-identical images, which is acceptable only as a build placeholder; in production the two examples must show a substantive, legible difference or the format's core teaching mechanism fails.

Do not drop the two-tone accent color on the title slide's emphasis keyword -- losing that highlight collapses the cover into flat unstyled text and removes the scroll-stopping cue the format depends on.

Do not omit, skip, or reorder the two-digit sequential numbering on any tip slide -- the numbered-list structure is the format's core promise of a complete, ordered reference, and a gap or repeat breaks that promise.

Do not replace the closing comment/heart/save engagement-icon row with a link-in-bio or 'follow me' call to action -- this format's CTA is on-platform participation (commenting a tip), not traffic redirection off-platform.
wrong_reading_locks_meaning: Do not treat design as mere ornamentation -- PRM-BUS-001 enforces visual guidance as attention control.
Do not disconnect layout hierarchy from reading order -- PRM-PSY-018 respects cognitive processing flow.
